claims.text: Two techniques: hyperpronation or supination-flexion. Neither needs equipment, sedation or a splint.
claims.quote: A hyperpronation or a supination-flexion technique may be used to reduce a radial head subluxation (nursemaid elbow). These techniques are safe and require no special equipment, assistants, analgesia/sedation, or post-procedure immobilization.

claims.text: Hyperpronation: rapidly hyperpronate the forearm. Some experts then flex the elbow.
claims.quote: For the hyperpronation technique , rapidly hyperpronate the forearm. Some experts recommend further flexion of the elbow immediately after hyperpronation.

claims.text: Supination-flexion: in one motion, supinate the forearm, then fully flex the elbow.
claims.quote: For the supination-flexion technique , using one continuous motion, rapidly and firmly supinate the forearm, then fully flex the elbow.

claims.text: Hyperpronation may hurt less and succeed more often.
claims.quote: The hyperpronation technique may cause less pain than the supination-flexion technique and may also have a higher rate of successful reduction.

claims.text: A thumb over the radial head feels the click of a successful reduction.
claims.quote: Placing the thumb over the radial head may facilitate recognition of a successful reduction via the palpable click or pop.
